text: LANE A SLICE 1 at exact SHA f0840c1ca9c23b277eaa2241ee43a43783a5a36b on lane/ea-unified-storefront-20260821 (pushed, base c371201). FILES: server/research/early-access/release/storefront-view.ts + new unified-storefront-scope.test.ts. 206 tests pass across server/research/early-access/release, tsc clean. NOTHING CHANGES YET - the route still asks for released_units; this makes the wider scope SAFE TO ASK FOR. WHAT SHIPPED: storefront units now carry a 'featured' mark computed against the release ledger by the caller, so the founder-released set stays legible once it stops being the FILTER. Merchandising carries no authority - tests assert a featured unit is not more buyable and an unfeatured one not less. SAFETY PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED: scope decides VISIBILITY AND NOTHING ELSE. A row not purchasable under released_units is not purchasable under 'all'; it becomes visible in its truthful held state with blockers, no price, no basis. purchasableCount is identical across both scopes. SEAM FINDING FOR YOU (the reason to read this): toUnit returns purchasable for ANY row Product Control has cleared (row.purchasable === blockers.length === 0), release or no release. Such a row is purchasable under BOTH scopes AND is currently INVISIBLE under released_units despite being sellable. So widening the scope does not merely reveal held rows - it PUBLISHES EVERY PRODUCT-CONTROL-CLEARED ROW. That is a founder readiness decision, not a merchandising side effect, and it is the actual gate on the unified storefront. Also note EA's row.purchasable is blockers-empty, i.e. full operational readiness incl. supplier/lot/COA - exactly what founder rule 5 says must NOT gate ACCEPTING an order. So the unified storefront must take its CTA from the canonical pathway (customer-pathway.ts / pathway-authority.ts), not from EA purchasable; both were unmerged when I wrote this.
